subject: Dedicated Capacity: throughput contingency & GPU mix playbook
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@orion-analytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orion-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 15, 2027 at 09:12 AM -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity RFP — throughput targets and GPU mix questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Quick background: Orion Analytics is evaluating a 12-month dedicated capacity commitment to support our conversational products (multi-tenant across three internal teams). High-level targets:~5M generated tokens/day, typical inference payloads are 128 tokens, peak 120 concurrent qps during business hours, and we need a P95 latency target under 800ms for typical prompts. We also have periodic heavy-batch scoring jobs overnight (throughput-focused).

The RFP asks for:
- recommended GPU families/mix to meet these mixed latency/throughput targets;
- suggested reservation sizing for a 12-month commitment with a 20% runway for growth;
- fallback/contingency plan if primary GPU capacity is constrained (how you degrade gracefully);
- expected lead time to provision dedicated capacity and any geographic constraints;
- SLA matrix (latency, uptime, credits) and pricing bands for baseline vs burst.

I've attached a clean copy of our RFP and the spreadsheet with our sample traffic profile (20270115_orion_rfp.pdf).

Can you confirm you received this and provide a preliminary sizing/strategy by early next week?

Best,
Lara Chen
Director, Platform Procurement
Orion Analytics


From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orion-analytics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 15, 2027 at 11:07 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity RFP — throughput targets and GPU mix questions

On Fri, Jan 15, 2027 at 09:12 AM Lara Chen <lara.chen@orion-analytics.com> wrote:
> Thanks for taking this RFP...

Hi Lara — thanks, got the RFP and the traffic workbook. Attached is a concise preliminary playbook to start the conversation (redwood_gpu_mix_workbook_jonas_v1.xlsx). High-level summary below — this is meant to be conservative and to leave options open for cost vs latency trade-offs.

Preliminary recommendation (based on the sample profile):
- Baseline pool (steady, latency-sensitive): 60% H100 (SXM) nodes — target for low P95 latency on long-context requests.
- Secondary pool (cost-sensitive mixed/throughput): 30% A100 (80GB) PCIe nodes — good balance for throughput and memory.
- Auxiliary burst/capacity lane: 10% L4 (32GB) / L40-equivalent instances for low-cost scale-out for batch scoring and non-critical workloads.

Sizing & headroom guidance:
- For your 5M tokens/day and 120 qps peak, we estimate an initial committed pool sized to handle ~80% of peak steady load with autoscaled burst into the auxiliary lane to cover spiky periods. That maps to an initial commitment equivalent to ~12 H100-equivalent slots (we provide the workbook with exact token-to-GPU mapping per model family).
- Recommend adding a 20% reserved headroom on top of modeled steady demand to simplify SLOs and avoid frequent burst usage.

Fallback / graceful degradation:
- Primary fallback is model variant routing: route latency-critical requests to smaller quantized variants (4-bit) with slightly degraded quality but consistent latency.
- Secondary fallback is regional routing to a compatible Dedicated pool in a second AZ/region (if you enable multi-region dedicated) or to Redwood Hosted fallthrough with contractual bandwidth caps.
- For scoring jobs, queue + batch backpressure with prioritized scheduling ensures user-facing requests keep low latency.

Provisioning timeline and constraints:
- If contract signed and a commitment SKU selected, we can provision a dedicated pool in ~3 weeks for us-west-2; cross-region provisioning may add 1–2 weeks depending on availability.

SLA and pricing bands:
- Attached is a starter SLA matrix (sla_matrix_scenarioA_v1.csv) with P95 latency targets per workload class, uptime %, and credit bands. Pricing bands are in the workbook.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Confirm which models you'll serve (list in the workbook) and peak sequence lengths.
2) We convert the preliminary sizing into a formal SOW and a staged provisioning plan (canary -> ramp).
3) Kickoff a technical workshop with our Serving and Reliability teams to validate KV cache, batching, and network topology.

I'll loop in Marcus and Evelyn to confirm operational notes. Let me know a good time for a 60-minute workshop early next week.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0134

Attachments: redwood_gpu_mix_workbook_jonas_v1.xlsx, sla_matrix_scenarioA_v1.csv

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, Jan 16, 2027 at 10:02 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity RFP — internal sizing notes

Jonas — quick internal notes from runbook review: 
- H100-heavy mix is appropriate for Orion's latency targets, but call out cost delta vs A100; add an explicit optional configuration that increases A100 share by 30% to cut run-rate ~18% while keeping P95 within tolerances for most prompts.
- For the 4-bit fallback path: we should quantify expected quality delta on the RFP's canonical prompts and include a small eval set in the SOW — put that in the workbook.
- Recommend we mandate a 20% emergency burst reserve (paid at a lower commitment premium) that Orion can trigger for short windows to avoid SLA hits during product launches.
- Operational ask: ensure KV cache warmup plan is documented for canary -> ramp to avoid cold-cache tail latency. Add a checklist to commitment_scenarios_playbook.pdf.

I'll draft the technical appendix for canary ramp and the model-variant routing diagram. Karthik — can you price the alternative A100-weighted tier and the emergency burst premium?

-Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, Jan 16, 2027 at 15:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity RFP — provisioning & SLAs

Adding ops constraints for the proposed plan: 
- Provisioning: us-west-2 (primary) available, typical lead time 3 weeks; multi-AZ redundancy included in the SOW.
- Canary plan: 1-week canary at 10–15% traffic, then 2-week ramp to 60–70% before full cutover. Cold-starts: plan for an initial KV pre-warm step to reduce early tail latency.
- SLA targets to propose to customer: 99.9% uptime monthly, P95 latency targets: 350ms for short-context (<256 tokens), 800ms for typical 512-token flows. Credits are tiered: 1% credit for partial P95 misses, 5% for sustained outage windows per the attached CSV.
- Compliance: include audit log retention policy (90 days default) and optional extended logs for an additional fee.

I'll join the workshop; avail Tue/Wed next week.

Evelyn Hart
Director, Reliability Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orion-analytics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 18, 2027 at 16:37 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal and next steps (Orion Analytics)

Hi Lara — following internal review we've consolidated a proposal and three commitment scenarios (attached). Key points: 

1) GPU mix options (attached workbook):
   - Scenario A (low-latency): 70% H100 / 25% A100 / 5% L4 — recommended if P95 is critical across long contexts.
   - Scenario B (balanced): 50% H100 / 40% A100 / 10% L4 — cost/latency balance (recommended by Redwood for most customers).
   - Scenario C (cost-first): 30% H100 / 60% A100 / 10% L4 — lowers run-rate, adds slightly higher P95 but keeps throughput.

2) Reservation sizing: workbook includes exact slot counts and the mapping to your traffic profile. Recommendation: sign up for Scenario B with a 20% headroom buffer; we can convert to Scenario A within the first 60 days if you validate latency with production traffic.

3) Contingency & fallbacks:
   - Model-variant routing to quantized 4-bit variants for non-critical paths.
   - Emergency burst lane (paid) that can be triggered for launches — we propose a 20% burst block that can be enabled within 2 hours.
   - Multi-region DR: optional; adds 1–2 week provisioning lead time and additional commit.

4) SLA & provisioning timeline:
   - Provisioning: ~3 weeks after contract + SOW sign for us-west-2.
   - SLA: 99.9% uptime, tiered credits; P95 latency targets as discussed. See sla_matrix_scenarioA_v1.csv for details.

Next steps (action items):
- Action (Orion): confirm the primary model families to be served and provide 3 canonical prompt examples and a small eval set (we'll use for quantization regressions). Requested by Jan 24.
- Action (Redwood): Marcus to provide the A100-weighted pricing tier; Evelyn to share canary runbook; Jonas to prepare SOW draft.
- Proposed kickoff: Jan 31st (60-min readiness + SOW review).

I've attached the workbook and the playbook PDF with the canary checklist and operational notes (commitment_scenarios_playbook.pdf).

If that timeline works, I'll get the SOW draft to Procurement and schedule the workshop.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
